reproduction_target: Genomic analysis comparing an improved short-nascent-strand sequencing protocol (iSNS-seq) with traditional SNS-seq (tSNS-seq) in S. cerevisiae: Bowtie2 alignment to sacCer3 plus custom spike-in 'chromosomes', SAMtools dedup/filter, MACS3 peak calling, bedGraph->bigWig coverage tracks, reprocessing of published ORC ChIP-seq / OK-seq / FORK-seq datasets into comparable origin call sets (OEM/RFD via sciaratools2 + switchblade), benchmarking against OriDB known origins with a custom python script (originsense.py), UMAP feature analysis of peak properties, transcription-level correlation in R, and reanalysis of published Drosophila tSNS-seq and C. elegans tSNS tiling-array data with DeepTools. Wet-lab work (oligo lambda-exo kinetics assays, SNSmimic/BKGmimic construct synthesis, yeast genomic DNA extraction, sucrose-gradient size selection, lambda-exo/RecJf enrichment, NEBNext library prep and NovaSeq sequencing) is out of computational-reproduction scope.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool-invocation from the 'Sequence data analysis', 'Benchmarking against known replication origins', 'Enriched feature analyses', 'Transcriptome analysis' and 'Analysis of other genome-wide tSNS studies' Methods sections. IGV visualization is folded into the bigWig conversion step; AWK reformatting is folded into the OK-seq OEM step; SAMtools/BEDtools invocations inside the reanalysis steps are folded into their parent step. Wet-lab procedures counted in W, not verdicted. IMPORTANT liveness finding recorded below: the paper's blanket code statement points to https://github.com/MiikoSokka/iSNS-seq, which returns HTTP 404 (the GitHub user exists but this repository does not); only the second, narrower repository https://github.com/JohnUrban/iSNS-seq (cited in-line for the OK-seq, FORK-seq and benchmarking steps) resolves. Per protocol, this is recorded verbatim and reflected in the code axis; no substitute repository was searched for.

steps.label: Alignment of iSNS-seq/tSNS-seq fastq to sacCer3 reference with SNSmimic and BKGmimic spike-ins added as extra 'chromosomes', Bowtie 2.5.3 (--maxins 1000, --local, --dovetail, --soft-clipped-unmapped-tlen, -D 500, -R 3, -N 0, -L 19, -i C,1,0, --score-min C,40,0)
SAMtools 1.22.1 duplicate marking and filtering (remove unmapped/duplicate/low-quality/orphan reads; keep concordant pairs, -F1028 -f3 -q2)
Peak calling per replicate with MACS 3.0.3 callpeak, no control file (-f BAMPE --mfold 2 100 -q 0.05, --bdg fragment-pileup bedGraph used as coverage track)
bedGraph -> bigWig conversion with UCSC bedGraphToBigWig 2.10 and visualization in IGV (IGV version unstated)
Reprocessing of published ORC ChIP-seq (NCBI SRA SRR1261246, SRR1261247) with the same Bowtie2/SAMtools pipeline and MACS 3.0.2 peak calling (--mfold 2 100 --keep-dup 1 -q 0.001)

OK-seq (SRA SRR364781, SRR364782) origin definition via OEM: bowtie2 (--very-sensitive-local --soft-clipped-unmapped-tlen), SAMtools (view -q 2 -F 4 -f 3), BEDtools genomecov -bga -strand +/- -pc, varStepBdgToSingleStepBdg.py from sciaratools2, AWK reformatting, strandSwitchMetrics.py from the switchblade suite for RFD/OEM in 10 kb windows, positive-zone maxima as origin summits

FORK-seq origin definition from published single-molecule nanopore initiation events: BEDtools clusterBed -d 5000, groupby (-grp 4 -opCols 1,2,3,4 -ops distinct,min/mean/median,max,count), AWK mid-point computation, median mid-point selected as single-bp origin, 500 bp flanks, rank sort by number of initiation events
Known-origin reference set from the OriDB database ('confirmed'/'likely'/'dubious' classes); no OriDB release version or access date stated
Random-shuffle null model: peak intervals randomly reassigned to new positions on the same chromosome; shuffling tool, seed and iteration count not stated in prose

Benchmarking of SN / PPV / F-score and binomial expected-overlap statistics across iSNS-seq, tSNS-seq, ORC, OK-seq, FORK-seq and shuffled sets, using the top 390 rank-sorted peaks with 500 bp flanks, automated by custom python script originsense.py (https://github.com/JohnUrban/iSNS-seq); no script version/commit, no python or dependency versions stated

Enriched-feature matrix and UMAP: BEDtools nuc GC content per narrowPeak region, BEDtools closest -t all distance-to-nearest-feature from peak summits, features from ensGene.v101.gtf downloaded from UCSC, Z-score normalization + one-hot encoding, python umap-learn 0.5.7 (n_neighbors=30, min_dist=0.15, metric='manhattan', random_state=42), replicates combined and analysis run blind to replicate

Transcription-level correlation: poly(A) transcriptome GSE162197 converted to bedGraph and averaged over six replicates, log2 transform + z-scoring, zero-value rows removed, two-tailed Spearman rank correlation with exact p-values disabled, regression/scatterplots in R with ggplot2; R and ggplot2 versions unstated

Drosophila tSNS-seq reanalysis: SRA SRR1791682 mapped with Bowtie2 to dm3 using the original study's parameters (-N 1 -L 22), SAMtools sorting, BEDtools genomecov -bga -split read depth, bigWig conversion, comparison with published S2 peak calls (GEO GSE65692), and Liftoff mapping of Drosophila r6.64 annotations to dm3; Liftoff/BEDtools/SAMtools versions unstated

C. elegans tSNS NimbleGen tiling-array reanalysis (GEO GSE86651, platform GPL16504): use of pre-computed log2(Cy5/Cy3) ratios plus independent recomputation from raw 'pair' files with median normalization, averaging across replicates, BLAST validation of probe coordinates against genome build WS180, annotations from WormBase; no tool versions, no BLAST parameters, no WormBase release stated

tRNA-gene metaprofile heatmaps/profiles with DeepTools computeMatrix (--regionBodyLength 150 --beforeRegionStartLength 3000 --afterRegionStartLength 3000; --binSize 1 for Drosophila, --binSize 10 for pre-computed C. elegans ratios, --binSize 50 for raw log2 ratio heatmaps/profiles); DeepTools version unstated, plotting command not stated

headline.static_readiness: 0/15 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 6 of 15 computational steps (C1-C5, C11) reach RI at stage-1: raw data are publicly deposited (ENA PRJEB95115; reused SRA/GEO accessions), parameters are unusually complete in prose, and exact version pins exist for the core pipeline (Bowtie 2.5.3, SAMtools 1.22.1, MACS 3.0.3/3.0.2, bedGraphToBigWig 2.10, umap-learn 0.5.7, ensGene.v101 annotation). Those steps stay at RI rather than R-star because there is no environment closure (no lockfile, container digest, conda env, or tagged release) and because the code axis cannot exceed 'reconstructable' at prose level. The remaining 9 steps cap at NI on the version axis: BEDtools, DeepTools, Liftoff, BLAST, R/ggplot2, python, and the sciaratools2 / switchblade helper repositories are all cited without versions or commits, and OriDB / WormBase releases are unpinned. A material ceiling is the code-liveness failure: the paper's blanket statement 'all code used to perform the analyses described in this study is available at https://github.com/MiikoSokka/iSNS-seq' resolves to HTTP 404, so the only reachable code covers the comparison/benchmarking analyses (JohnUrban/iSNS-seq), not the primary iSNS-seq/tSNS-seq processing, UMAP, or transcriptome steps.
headline.coverage: 15 computational steps assessed from Methods prose plus the reachable repository landing page and README prose (JohnUrban/iSNS-seq, code/README.md); 6 wet-lab steps counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope. Data availability statement present and specific; code availability is stated in Methods and Data availability but the primary URL is dead.
